The spreadsheet, with every winner since TI2. Secret currently holds The Belt.

The twitter account, @dota2belt, where I will track The Belt forward

In boxing and wrestling, the championship title gets passed from athlete to athlete, a lineal title. I have tracked the Dota title as if it passed from team to team, much like the NFL Belt or Unofficial Football World Championship. The first team to hold the championship was Na'Vi after TI1 completed. The team to beat them would then claim The Belt.

The Rules Of The Belt:

  1. The winner of the first International claims The Belt.
  2. If the holder of The Belt loses a match, they give The Belt to their opponent.
  3. If The Belt's holder loses the second game of a BO2 series, they lose The Belt.
  4. Any match in Dota 2 on a ticketed tournament featuring the majority of members of that team playing under the banner of that team that holds The Belt is a title match.
  5. If the holder of The Belt disbands, the team with the most players from the previous team keeps The Belt.
  6. If The Belt's roster loses a majority of their members to another team, that team holds The Belt.
  7. Standins are ignored for the purpose of the above rules.
  8. If The Belt is lost, The Belt is claimed by the winner of the next tournament featuring top caliber teams from both East and West.

Pre-TI2 disclaimer

Tickets didn't exist back in the day. Some teams competed on Dota Allstars and 2 at the same time. While I am not certain as to where The Belt traveled after Na'Vi's victory, a few assumptions guided my thinking. Na'Vi wins every tournament entered after TI1 for a long while, seemingly not until the Starchampionship (Starladder Season 0, if you're counting), but the winning team The Retry disbands right after. I had a writeup tracking it between several teams, now lost, but the gist is that every TI2 caliber team enters the BTS World Tour tournament, where CLG wins, and The Belt can be assumed to enter TI2, where IG wins, and the reckoning begins.

Take Five

Take Five was a stack formed to enter the EMS One tournament in 2013. Its members are, according to Liquipedia, Demon, Mason, Pandaego, , and DarkFalco. They win the tournament qualifier, then disband. The next day, a majority of members are seen in Team Dignitas, and Mason goes awol until he begins standing in for EG. Dignitas takes The Belt the next day.

Notes

This is obviously not meant to be a general assessment of team strength over time. One slipup in a BO1 group stage (see Alliance post-TI3 dropping a game to Revenge (now Not Today!) and PR) can make you lose The Belt. The Belt has made several visits to low-tier tournaments, where teams like Dignitas, Take Five, House of Gamers, MUFC, and Union Gaming have held The Belt. In addition, holding The Belt for a long time may not indicate pure skill. Post TI2 there was a drought of games in China and IG cut their tournaments down significantly. There is included in the chart the days The Belt has been held, as well as the amount of matches The Belt has survived without being lost. TI4 DK's 10 match defense is a feat in itself, and a stronger feat than IG's 75 day defense post TI2. A history of The Belt is a history of competitive Dota 2, and is worth several writeups in itself.

The Future

I intend to post The Belt's progress daily and throughout TI5 and beyond on Twitter, @dota2belt. Secret currently holds The Belt after their performance in ESL Frankfurt 2015. This model may also be applicable to other esport titles, and if you do replicate it for other games do let me know.
